plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. The heads track the sun in their youth and face east at maturity. Widely cultivated for seeds, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July-September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across the United States, Europe, Russia, and Ukraine
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west each day, a movement called heliotropism, and then reset overnight to face east.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil and is a magnet for bees and butterflies. It is harvested for essential oils, sachets, and culinary use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak bloom from June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the Pacific Northwest of the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and Romans added it to their bathwater, which is where its name likely comes from, from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Epilobium angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that forms spires of vivid magenta-pink flowers which bloom from the bottom of the spike upward. It colonizes burned or disturbed land, carpeting hillsides in color. It is a vital nectar source for bees and a source of honey.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to September in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Boreal and temperate regions of North America, Europe, and Asia, including Alaska, Canada, Scandinavia, and Siberia
plants.funFact: Fireweed was among the first plants to regrow after the 1980 Mount St. Helens eruption, and locals say that when the blooms reach the top of the stalk, summer is nearly over.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round leaves that rise above the water and spectacular, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a water-repellent surface. It is cultivated in ponds and revered in many cultures as a symbol of purity.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, peaking July to August in temperate Asia
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; widely grown in India, China, Japan, and Vietnam
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds can remain viable for centuries; one seed about 1,300 years old was successfully germinated after being recovered from a dry lakebed in China.
